title: Earl Trusclair teaches saxophone fingering; end of Pete Herman's job
summary: Earl Trusclair showed Handy saxophone fingering in exchange for clarinet fingering; the Pete Herman's job lasted about a year before Ridgely broke up the band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I was playing clarinet. I was doing clarinet. And what about the name of Earl? His name was Earl Trusclair. He's the first man that ever showed me any finger on a saxophone. We alternated. He showed me my finger on the saxophone and I showed him his finger on the clarinet. And that's the only thing anybody ever showed me about a saxophone. Oh, no. Nobody never showed me nothing about a clarinet, but on the saxophone, that's the only fella ever showed me anything. He showed me how to finger it. And other than that, I didn't have any more. That's all I needed, you know, because if I learned how to finger it, I could learn how to play it. All I wanted to know how to finger it, you know. And we played, we stayed down there at Pete Harmon for, I guess, a year or something. That was right after Solistan the band. And then Baby Ridgely broke the band up.
